notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Website states wines are produced using 'clean, vegan, gluten-free winemaking' practices

Multiple bistro menu items explicitly labeled Vegetarian, Vegan & Gluten-Friendly, Vegetarian & Gluten-Friendly, or Gluten-Friendly (e.g., Garden Bistro Salad 'Vegan & Gluten-Friendly', Roasted Delicata Squash Salad 'Vegetarian & Gluten-Friendly')

notes.Takeout: Wine available for direct retail purchase from the winery shop; full selection including special old vintages, seasonal specials, and case-lot options sold on-site. Cash or cheque only — no cards accepted

notes.Vegetarian / vegan / GF: Veggie burger option listed on taphouse menus at multiple locations: 'BEEF OR VEGGIE BURGER W/ FRIES'
Dedicated gluten-free beer line including Forager Lager and Forager Pale Ale, both award-winning; gluten-free section on taphouse menu
FAQ confirms vegan and dairy-free food options; gluten-free food options described as limited but accommodated where possible
notes.Covered bike parking: FAQ explicitly states 'covered bike parking in front of the taproom.'

wow_cap: The 'garden that love built' — heritage show garden with teahouse.
Zodiac whale-watching tours from Steveston village.
Railway and pioneer museum in one of BC's finest surviving Canadian Pacific stations.
55-acre world-class botanical garden in Shaughnessy.
Award-winning Haida cultural centre built as a traditional village at ancient Kay Llnagaay.
Adventure base near Whistler: whitewater rafting, ziplines, and aerial courses.
Reifel Bird Sanctuary: 300 species of birds on Westham Island wetlands.
2010 Olympic bobsleigh and luge track; free viewing tours, paid summer bobsleigh rides.
BC's planetarium since 1968; full-dome theatre, moon rocks, and live science shows.
137-metre heated saltwater outdoor pool on Kitsilano Beach, among North America's longest.
Museum in Vancouver's old morgue; walk through the authentic 1970s autopsy suite.
British sweets shop with Dickens-themed museum rooms and high tea.
Canada's only Indigenous academic library; Interior Salish pit-house architecture, open to all.
Skyride gondola base of Grouse Mountain's summit attractions.
Free pavilion housing Engine 374, which pulled Canada's first transcontinental train into Vancouver in 1887.
Restored 1914 sternwheeler SS Sicamous, moored on Penticton's Okanagan Lake shore.
1859 steamboat captain's home, one of BC's oldest houses.
Canada's country-music hall of fame, in downtown Merritt.
Jet-boat grizzly tours from Blue River, with a floating rainforest restaurant.
First full-scale Ming Dynasty classical garden outside China, in historic Chinatown.
Free cabinet-of-wonders museum of natural history and world artifacts, Maple Bay.
Gold-rush roadhouse ranch on the Cariboo Wagon Road; twenty original buildings from 1861.
Tofino eco-tour pioneer since 1986; zodiac whale watching and Hot Springs Cove.
North Coast museum of Tsimshian history and art, in a monumental longhouse building.
World's oldest intact passenger sternwheeler (1898), a National Historic Site on Kaslo's waterfront.
BC's largest public art collection, anchored by an 1889 mansion.
Base of the Grouse Grind, 'nature's StairMaster' up Grouse Mountain.
Tofino's famous surf school; lessons and rentals for all levels.
Non-profit Salish Sea aquarium on the Sidney waterfront.
Working heritage fishing village at the Fraser's mouth.
Night walk through illuminated forest with light installations and storytelling.
95 heritage trains including the Royal Hudson, with rides.
Aerial ropes courses and bungy jumping over the Nanaimo River.
Kamloops' oldest church, restored on Tk'emlups lands with its gilded altar intact.
Urban inlet at the heart of Vancouver, ringed by the car-free seawall path.
Indigenous-led kayak tours and rentals from Pender and Mayne islands.
Community-owned natural mineral hot pools in the Kuskanax Valley, 14 paved km from Nakusp.
Roy Henry Vickers' cedar longhouse gallery, a Tofino landmark since 1986.
Hands-on science museum in the Expo 86 geodesic dome on False Creek.
Open-air forestry museum in Duncan; ride the steam train through a 1930s logging camp.
Shakespeare festival in waterfront tents at Vanier Park, June to September.
1906 general store museum with costumed interpreters and campground.
Nisga'a Nation museum of repatriated regalia and art in the Nass Valley.
Public pool fed by Harrison's natural mineral hot springs.
Observatory visitor centre at the 1918 Plaskett Telescope National Historic Site.
Vancouver's highest point: quarry gardens, an arboretum, and panoramic city-and-mountain views.
Chemainus' professional festival theatre, anchor of the mural town's renaissance.
Boardwalk nature centre in Canada's rare antelope-brush desert near Osoyoos.
1941 Art Deco concert hall on Granville Street, a National Historic Site.
Short climb to the PENTICTON sign viewpoint over both Okanagan and Skaha lakes.
Wildlife rehabilitation park in Kamloops, home of the world's only Kermode bear in care.
Tla-o-qui-aht-guided boat trips to Meares Island's ancient cedars.
Living-history museum at one of BC's oldest cattle ranches, north of Vernon.
1852 home of Dr. J.S. Helmcken, among BC's oldest surviving houses.
Free waterfront heritage shipyard village in Steveston.
Monumental First Nations totem poles on the Stanley Park seawall; free, open-air.
Gondola to Howe Sound summit views and a suspension bridge.
Indigenous-led canoe tours on False Creek with Coast Salish guides; carving demonstrations.
Six-line guided zipline above Kokanee Creek canyon, with views to Kootenay Lake.
Classic diorama attraction at the Empress: 85 miniature worlds, tiny working sawmill.
Interactive art arcade of rebuilt vintage machines you're meant to touch.
50-metre bungee jumps over the glacial Cheakamus River in a basalt canyon.
Protected old-growth forest with 900-year cedars; free guided tours by the conservancy society.
Arts and recreation centre in a converted 1888 CPR roundhouse in Yaletown.
World-famous 55-acre gardens in a former quarry at Brentwood Bay; a National Historic Site.
Ahousaht-owned tours: whales, bears, and Hot Springs Cove from Tofino.
The last wooden steam sternwheeler, moored at New Westminster Quay.
Naval and military museum on CFB Esquimalt, Canada's oldest Pacific base.
Hatley Park's free Italian, Japanese, and rose gardens around the castle.
Aviation museum at Victoria Airport, home of the giant Hawaii Martin Mars flying boat.
Coal baron Dunsmuir's 1890 castle, a National Historic Site above Victoria.
A stolen 1970s tractor slowly swallowed by Burns Bog.
Tsleil-Waututh canoe tours and kayak rentals on Indian Arm.
Lək̓ʷəŋən-guided canoe and walking tours from Victoria's Inner Harbour.
Natural history museum under a 26 m blue whale skeleton.
Indigenous-led coastal gardens with rainforest trails and a carving studio.
Free 10-acre 1920s heritage village with carousel and interurban tram.
1911 hydroelectric powerhouse preserved as a museum at Stave Falls.
Ride restored interurban railcars from historic Cloverdale Station.
BC's 1898 Parliament Buildings on the Inner Harbour; free public tours.
UBC centre preserving Indian Residential School history; archives and dialogue space, open to public.
Father Pandosy's 1859 mission, the Okanagan's oldest European settlement site.
Victoria's Victorian-era city hall, a National Historic Site on Centennial Square.
Gold Rush heritage site in Yale: Creighton House, Ward House, and an 1863 church.
Artist-run centre since 1973 in a heritage false-front building; media and performance art.
Ten-building village museum of BC Doukhobor life 1908-1938; 1,600 artifacts, guided tours.
Restored Trans-Canada Limited railcars and fossil galleries at the Cranbrook History Centre.
Farm near Kelowna airport where you hand-feed kangaroos, wallabies, and capybaras.
Indoor 200 m wooden velodrome — the only one in the Pacific Northwest.
Canada's largest civic history museum, exploring Vancouver's communities from Vanier Park.
Canada's largest aquarium, in Stanley Park; marine research centre since 1956.
Preserved salmon cannery telling the west coast fishery's story.
Arthur Erickson's landmark hilltop campus with Metro Vancouver views.
St'át'imc-guided tours of the Bridge River fishing grounds and an 80-pit-house village site.
Indigenous-led ethnobotany walks and paddle tours rooted in Coast Salish teachings.
Canada's major western art museum; Emily Carr collection in a landmark former courthouse.
Visitor centre beside the Terex Titan, one of the world's largest trucks, on Highway 3.
1912 lighthouse and National Historic Site at the tip of old-growth Lighthouse Park.
Victoria whale-watching tours into the Salish Sea for over 33 years.
National museum and cultural centre of Japanese Canadian history.
World-renowned Northwest Coast First Nations collection in Arthur Erickson's landmark UBC building.
Famous 137 m suspension bridge with treetop and cliff walkways.
Kelowna's heritage museum: syilx history, a recreated Chinatown, and valley geology.
Museum in Vancouver's oldest building, an 1865 sawmill store; Great Fire artifacts.
Photography gallery in an award-winning waterfront building.
Canada's oldest university botanical garden, with canopy walkway.
Opulent 1927 concert hall, home of the Vancouver Symphony; National Historic Site.
Beloved BC Hydro lake recreation area with beaches and trails.
Famous 8 km clifftop trail through rainforest and headlands at Ucluelet.
Victorian coastal fort and Canada's west coast's oldest lighthouse, near Victoria.
